title: Orange Shirt Day and the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
dek: September 30 is Orange Shirt Day and Canada's National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, a day to remember residential school survivors.
keywords: national day for truth and reconciliation
body: Today, September 30, is Orange Shirt Day. In Canada it is also the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, and this year marks the sixth time the country has observed it.

Orange Shirt Day was founded in 2013 by a residential school survivor. People wear orange as a visible act of remembrance, solidarity, and tribute to survivors and to the children who never came home, including the thousands identified in unmarked graves. Many of the shirts carry the words Every Child Matters.

The residential school system was built to separate Indigenous children from their families, languages and cultures. Its effects are still felt today, in families on both sides of the border. It is a painful history, and I think the least any of us can do is take the time to learn it and listen to the people who lived it.

For many people outside Canada, this day is not on the work calendar. Even so, it is worth setting aside a few minutes this morning to read, reflect and pay attention. Many schools, cities and organizations share resources and host gatherings today, including the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation.
If you have an orange shirt, consider wearing it today. Then spend ten minutes reading a survivor's story in their own words.
